newsitem.title: INDIA: India proposes cutting rayon grade wood pulp duty. [CORRECTED 11:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: India proposes cutting rayon grade wood pulp duty. [CORRECTED 11:55 GMT]

text.p: The Indian government on Wednesday proposed slashing the customs duty on rayon grade wood pulp to 10 percent (Correct from five percent) from 25 percent.
In July, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram had proposed cutting the duty to five percent from 25 percent.
Chidambaram told the lower house of parliament on Wednesday that he had been told that such a steep reduction would no doubt reduce the cost of production of viscose fibre and yarn.
But, he said, it would hurt rayon grade wood pulp makers who market their entire production.
"I, therefore, propose to keep the reduction in the customs duty on rayon grade wood pulp from 25 percent to 10 percent," Chidambaram said.
